expectations.text: Uses a discriminated union keyed on the status field
expectations.evidence: type Subscription = | { status: "trialing"; trialEndDate: Date } | { status: "active"; renewalDate: Date } | ...

expectations.text: Each variant carries only its own fields, so e.g. a canceled subscription cannot hold a trial end date
expectations.evidence: "You cannot construct a subscription with mismatched fields — `{ status: "active", cancelReason: "..." }` won't typecheck"; each variant lists only its own fields with no optionals

expectations.text: Includes a compiler-enforced exhaustiveness check (assertNever or an equivalent never arm)
expectations.evidence: function assertNever(x: never): never { ... } ... default: return assertNever(sub);

expectations.text: Introduces distinct or branded types rather than bare strings for IDs
expectations.evidence: Branding is offered only for Date fields (TrialEndDate, GracePeriodEnd, RenewalDate); no subscription/customer ID field appears anywhere, and cancelReason refinement is a string-literal union, not an ID type

expectations.text: Provides a single transition function or otherwise constrains how state changes
expectations.evidence: Only `getNextBillingAction` (a read-only formatter) is provided; no transition function, no allowed-transition map, and no discussion of constraining state changes

expectations.text: Explicitly names which misuses the design makes impossible
expectations.evidence: "**What this prevents (Control rung):** - You cannot access `trialEndDate` without first narrowing to `status === "trialing"`..." plus the numbered Misuse Enumeration table

expectations.text: Avoids a bag-of-optional-fields interface as the primary recommendation
expectations.evidence: "**The bag-of-optionals trap**" is named as an anti-pattern; the recommendation is the discriminated union with "no optional bags"
